title: Dashboard
purpose: See notices from your repository’s administrators and the specimen, equipment and distribution work waiting for your roles.
summary: Notices from your repository's administrators and the specimen, equipment and distribution work waiting for your roles.

tasks.title: Start on the work that is waiting
steps: Find the queue under Your work queues.
Select its label to open the list of those items with the filter applied. Queues showing 0 have no link.

tasks.title: Open a recently stored specimen
steps: Under Recently stored, select the specimen ID.

good_to_know: Counts are live and match the rows the linked list shows.
Approval and review queues never count your own requests or submissions. Another person must decide them.
Limits, low levels and due dates are the ones your repository entered. The application sets none.
Announcements cannot be dismissed. They disappear when they end or are withdrawn.

items.label: Announcements
items.description: Current notices the repository’s administrators posted for staff appear first, newest first, each marked Notice or Important with a title and a plain-text message. They are the same for every role, cannot be dismissed, and disappear when they end or are withdrawn. Nothing appears when none is current. Announcements meant only for the sign-in page are not repeated here unless they were also posted for staff. Administrators manage them under Setup, Announcements.

items.label: Your work queues
items.description: Queues are grouped under Specimens, Equipment and Distribution. Each row names a kind of work, its count, the age of the oldest item (“just now” under a minute) and links to the matching list with the filter applied; the count is the number of rows that list shows. A queue with nothing waiting is one quiet line with a count of 0 and no link. Checked out: specimens out of storage now. Registered, not stored: available specimens with no storage position that are not checked out. On hold: specimens with an unreleased hold. Disposal requests awaiting my approval: shown only to people who hold the disposal approval permission, and counts requests made by other people. Approved disposals to record: shown to admin, manager and technician roles. Equipment queues follow the specimen ones: Readings outside limits without an excursion (admin, manager and technician roles; temperature readings outside the limits your repository set that no excursion covers yet), Open temperature excursions (open or awaiting review), Excursions awaiting my review (admin and manager roles; submitted by other people, never your own), LN2 vessels below their low level (the latest recorded level is below the level your repository set), Maintenance and calibration overdue (past the next due date recorded on the latest event) and Maintenance and calibration due in 30 days (the 30 days is a display choice, not a maintenance policy). Distribution queues follow: Requests awaiting my decision (only for people who hold the request decision permission and an admin, manager or technician role; counts submitted requests that you neither created nor submitted, while its link opens every request awaiting a decision), Approved requests with allocations to pick, Shipments packed, awaiting dispatch, and Dispatched shipments without a recorded receipt (admin, manager and technician roles), then for admin and manager roles Returns awaiting review (returned specimens stay on a use hold until reviewed), Withdrawals needing follow-up (withdrawals in effect with specimens in custody that have no hold from them, or a shipment of the participant’s material without recorded follow-up) and Agreements expiring or with reporting due within 60 days (executed agreements expiring in the next 60 days or with a reporting date passed or within 60 days; the 60 days is a display choice, and nothing expires or is enforced automatically except validity at dispatch). The limits, low levels and due dates are the ones your repository entered; the application sets none. When nothing is waiting the section says “Nothing is waiting for you” instead of a table of zeros.

items.label: Recently stored
items.description: The ten newest placements and check-ins, newest first, each with the specimen ID (which opens the specimen) and the position recorded at that time. Until specimens are stored it shows “No specimens stored yet”.

sections.title: Access and records
paragraphs: Every active account with a repository role (admin, manager, technician or viewer) can open the dashboard; an account without a role is refused. The page header names the repository. The dashboard has no search, sorting or paging controls and stores no tasks of its own: queue counts are live counts of the linked records.
Disposal approval and request decisions are separate per-person permissions; holding one adds its queue. Superuser status does not.
